title: Meta Agrees to Sweeping Changes to Restrict Kids’ Access to Its Apps as Part of Settlement with States
summary: Meta has agreed to implement significant changes to enhance child safety on Instagram and Facebook as part of an $18 billion settlement with 29 U.S. states. The measures, set to last for 10 years, include daily time limits, restrictive 'Night Mode,' non-algorithmic feeds, and stricter controls on notifications and content access for users under 18.
key_points: Meta will enforce a **daily two-hour time limit** for teens on Facebook and Instagram, cumulative across both apps, with parental override required to disable.
A **default 'Night Mode'** will block underage users from accessing the platforms between midnight and 6 a.m.
Teens can set a **non-algorithmic, chronological feed** as their default, with parental control over this setting.
**Notifications will be muted by default** during school hours (8 a.m.–3 p.m.), except for DMs and security alerts.
**Autoplay controls** will require deliberate user action (e.g., tapping/swiping) to view more content.
**Like/reaction counts** will be hidden by default for underage users.
Meta will **strengthen age-verification technology** to ensure teens receive appropriate protections, even if they falsify their age.
The company is **urging TikTok and YouTube** to adopt similar measures, with 30% of the settlement ($5.3B) contingent on their compliance.
Changes will apply automatically to users under 18 in participating U.S. states, pending judicial approval.
